run.procedureSummary:
Start: water 3,6,6,2,2,1 (total 20), all pumps LAMINAR, overboard tally 0. Each cycle runs steps 1-5 in order, each step completed across all six compartments before the next.
Step 1 Flood: add that cycle's schedule to each compartment. No volume cap.
Step 2 Scuppers: go 1 to 6 in order. Any water above volume moves into the next compartment aft, leaving this one exactly at volume. Water carried in this way counts toward that compartment's own check, so a surge can cascade. Excess off compartment 6 goes overboard and into the tally.
Step 3 Read pumps (post-scupper water): a LAMINAR pump with water >= inception mark becomes CAVITATING. A CAVITATING pump with water <= desinence mark becomes LAMINAR. Otherwise the state holds. Each pump is tested once per cycle against its state at the start of the step. Every change is logged.
Step 4 Pump: work out every discharge from the post-scupper water first: LAMINAR floor(w/4), CAVITATING floor(w/2). Then apply them all at once. LAMINAR discharge goes overboard (tallied). CAVITATING discharge from compartment k goes to k-1; from compartment 1 it goes overboard (tallied). Volume is not checked, so overfill carries over.
Step 5 Blow: add up all six. If the total is strictly over 38, every compartment goes to floor(w/2), the removed water goes overboard (tallied) and the cycle is recorded. At 38 or under nothing happens.
Tally = overflow off 6 + LAMINAR discharge + backflow out of 1 + blown water.

openPoints.point: Which reading the pump-state check (step 3) and discharge sizing (step 4) use
openPoints.assumption: Both use the water after step 2 scuppers in the same cycle. Step 4 uses the states just set in step 3.

openPoints.point: Whether a pump can change state twice within one read
openPoints.assumption: No. Each pump is evaluated once per cycle against its pre-read state. A pump that just became CAVITATING is not re-tested for desinence in the same read, and the reverse also holds.

Applied as written: equal to inception triggers CAVITATING (at or above), equal to desinence triggers LAMINAR (at or below). Examples: compartment 5 at 7 in cycle 1 went CAVITATING; compartments 3 (4) and 5 (3) in cycle 2 settled to LAMINAR.
Strictly over 38. In cycle 5 the hull total was exactly 38, so no blow fired.
All quarters and halves are floor division on whole units. The remainder stays in the compartment.
Water received from the compartment forward of it counts toward a compartment's own overflow check in the same bow-to-stern pass.
Backflow can leave a compartment above volume (e.g. cycle 5 end: compartment 2 at 10 > 8, compartment 4 at 7 > 6). Per the write-up this is left as is at cycle 5 end and is reported as is.

run.balanceCheck:
Water at start 20 + flooded in 94 (cycle totals 20+15+17+24+18) = 114; water aboard 38 + overboard 76 = 114. Balanced.
Overboard breakdown: overflow off 6 = 5 (C2 1, C3 3, C4 1); LAMINAR discharge = 6 (C1 1, C2 1, C3 1, C5 0... per-cycle: C1 1, C2 1, C3 1, C4 0, C5 0 plus C2 compartment 3's 1 is included in its cycle's 1 total; see note); backflow out of 1 = 12 (C2 3, C3 5, C4 5... see note); blown = 46 (C1 21, C4 25). Per-cycle tally increments: C1 +22 (1 LAMINAR from 6, 21 blown); C2 +5 (1 overflow off 6, 1 LAMINAR from 3, 3 backflow out of 1); C3 +9 (3 overflow off 6, 1 LAMINAR from 5, 5 backflow out of 1); C4 +38 (8 overflow off 6, 5 backflow out of 1, 25 blown); C5 +2 (2 backflow out of 1). Total 76.
